detail.abstract:
AI agents and institutional automation increasingly require public accountability, while many operational records must remain private due to personal data, trade secrets, contractual terms, security constraints, or audit boundaries. This paper introduces Two-Rail Verification, a public-private evidence-separation kernel for institutional AI and AI-agent governance. The proposed kernel distinguishes between a Public Rail, where public claims, status, version, timestamps, hashes, and verification routes can be placed, and a Private Rail, where raw records, personal data, cost structures, contracts, internal logs, secrets, and unpublished evidence remain protected.

The contribution is not a new cryptographic primitive, a certification scheme, or a production assurance claim. Rather, Two-Rail organizes existing concepts such as hashes, signatures, manifests, verification kits, verifiable credentials, selective disclosure, zero-knowledge proofs, transparency logs, audit trails, and assurance reports into an institutional evidence-separation discipline. The kernel is expressed through four minimal requirements: cross-rail write prohibition, verified public claims, a verifiable public surface, and an accountability interface.

The paper discusses the public-private evidence problem, adjacent technical and governance concepts, minimal public-surface design, use cases for AI agents and institutional records, and limitations. It does not claim third-party verification, complete signature coverage, legal compliance, safety guarantees, or an effective royalty-free patent pledge. Related patent applications may be pending, but any future patent pledge or license should be published separately with an effective date and stable URL.

title: The Dynamics of Random Purges
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Economics and UC Berkeley Haas School of Business, UC Berkeley Haas School of Business

detail.title: The Dynamics of Random Purges
detail.abstract: We study a novel dynamic infinite horizon game between a principal and a group of agents she wants to eliminate. Each period, the principal targets a subset of agents for elimination. Agents can protest and successful protest stops the principal forever. We contrast two classes of equilibria: in the first, the principal proposes to eliminate agents according to a pre-specified list, while in the second, the principal proposes to eliminate a uniformly random subset of agents each period. In the first case, the principal engages in at most one round of elimination. In the second case, the principal typically engages in many rounds of elimination, stopping at an endogenously determined cutoff. The principal approaches this cutoff at constrained maximum speed, eliminating as many agents as would be statically optimal each period. We discuss a number of illustrative cases, focusing on elite purges.

title: Income and Tax Consequences of Selling Ownership Stakes: Evidence from Major Shareholders of Private Firms in Canada
affiliations: and University of British Columbia

detail.title: Income and Tax Consequences of Selling Ownership Stakes: Evidence from Major Shareholders of Private Firms in Canada
detail.abstract: This paper assesses the income and tax consequences of selling ownership stakes in private companies using linked tax records of business owners in Canada. Comparing major shareholders who sell their entire stakes with matched counterparts who sell at a later time, we find large reductions in their overall income and taxes after selling their company, except for an initial spike in capital gains. Furthermore, they reduce their labor supply and wage income on average. We do not find evidence of serial entrepreneurship across ages or sectors, implying that business owners enjoy a “quiet life” after selling instead of starting new firms or remaining active in the labor market.

title: Curriculum Development in Academic Economics Education: Evidence from Dutch BSc Programmes in Economics and Business Economics (ca. 2010-2025) using Natural Language Processing

detail.abstract: This article examines curriculum development in Dutch undergraduate Economics and Business Economics from approximately 2010 to 2025, using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyse 5,393 courses across eight universities (extracted from online guides). A topic analysis employing non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and n-gram trend analysis on course objectives and descriptions provide systematic empirical evidence on how broader debates about economic paradigms, employability skills and pedagogical innovation are reflected in formalized curricula. The findings suggest both continuity and change: traditional economic theory, quantitative methods, and academic research skills remain dominant themes throughout the period, while topics related to employability skills, corporate governance, data science and real-world application seem to be on the rise. Programme-level analyses suggest that national higher education systems can accommodate curricular diversity within a common disciplinary framework, with institutional diWerences potentially linked to research specializations and strategic positioning. The NLP methodology developed here offers a replicable approach for studying curriculum change across different geographical contexts and academic disciplines, and contributes to evidence-based policy discussions in economics and higher education.

title: Intergenerational Discounting and Inequality
affiliations: University of Copenhagen - Department of Economics and University of St. Gallen

detail.title: Intergenerational Discounting and Inequality
detail.abstract: We study theories of intergenerational justice that disentangle ethical attitudes toward discounting  from ethical attitudes toward intergenerational inequalities. We call such criteria modular: each one is uniquely identified by a time-discounting function---capturing attitudes toward time---and a law-invariant aggregator---capturing attitudes toward inequality. We provide an axiomatic characterization of modularity and show its implications. Our framework nests the workhorse criteria used in applied work and yields large, tractable families of alternative criteria obtained by freely combining discounting and inequality attitudes.

detail.title: Analysis of the Factors Causing the Weakening of the Rupiah Exchange Rate and Its Impact on National Economic Stability
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the factors causing the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate and how it impacts the stability of the national economy. The method used is a qualitative descriptive literature study involving the analysis of scientific literature, official reports, and recent economic publications. The results of the study indicate that external factors, such as the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy, the strengthening of the US dollar, and global economic uncertainty, as well as domestic factors, such as inflation, the trade deficit, capital outflows, and fiscal conditions, contribute to the weakening of the rupiah. In addition to increasing export competitiveness, the weakening of the rupiah also has negative effects, including increased import costs, inflation, foreign debt, and pressure on national economic stability. Consequently, to strengthen Indonesia's economic fundamentals and maintain exchange rate stability, monetary and fiscal policies must work together.

title: Communities with Shared Futures: China and Latin America

detail.title: Communities with Shared Futures: China and Latin America
detail.abstract: The term "community with a shared future" denotes the highest level of diplomatic partnership and foreign relations under Chinese foreign policy. An argument could be made that when both economic and political factors are considered, Latin America is the closest region in the world to achieving the ideal of a region-wide community with a shared future with China. Brazil and Cuba have both signed bilateral agreements to join hands with China in a community with a shared future, and Brazil was also the first country that signed any kind of strategic partnership agreement with China back in 1993. The 33-member Community of Latin American and Caribbean States has met every three years with China to improve policy coordination, and the Chinese government has often characterized the goal of these meetings as the aspiration to build a community with a shared future. This article endeavors to explain why, despite nominally being part of "the West," Latin America is nonetheless diplomatically and economically closer to China than other areas of the "Global South."

title: Marriage Without Births: A Diaspora Margin of Fertility Decline——Evidence from Chinese and Korean Americans, 2008–2024
affiliations: Liaoning University

detail.title: Marriage Without Births: A Diaspora Margin of Fertility Decline——Evidence from Chinese and Korean Americans, 2008–2024
detail.abstract: Fertility has fallen sharply in China and South Korea, and this paper documents a parallel decline among Chinese and Korean Americans living in a markedly different socioeconomic environment. Using ACS and administrative birth records (NVSS) for 2008–2024, I characterize where this decline is located within the U.S. household life cycle. Age-standardized fertility rates among Chinese and Korean American women aged 25–44 fell by approximately 41 and 26 percent between 2016 and 2024, substan- tially more than among the principal U.S. comparison groups. Partnership measures changed by similar small magnitudes across Chinese and Korean women and the non- Hispanic white BA+ benchmark group, locating the fertility divergence after household formation. Within early marriage, the decline is disproportionately concentrated among coethnic dual-college couples. The Chinese triple-difference relative to the analogous non-Hispanic white cell is −4.6 percentage points, with the largest movement in 2023– 2024; the Korean differential is economically large but less precisely estimated. Within the focal cell, Chinese declines appear among U.S.-born, childhood-arrival, and adult- arrival women, making changing composition among recent adult immigrants an insuf- ficient explanation. The results do not identify a causal mechanism, but they locate a recent diaspora fertility decline at the marriage-to-birth margin and in households plausibly most exposed to intensive child-investment and dual-career pressures.

title: Survival-adjusted Terminal Nodes: Integrating BSVM™ into Real Options Valuation

detail.title: Survival-adjusted Terminal Nodes: Integrating BSVM™ into Real Options Valuation
detail.abstract: Real options valuation (ROV) inherits from the Gordon Growth Model a critical and undeclared assumption: that the firm underlying the option exists with certainty at the terminal node and generates cash flows in perpetuity. We demonstrate that this assumption-denoted S(T) = 1-is internally inconsistent with the simultaneous inclusion of an abandonment option, whose positive expected value requires S(T) < 1 by definition. We introduce the Business Survival Value Multiplier (BSVM™) as the correction mechanism: at the terminal node of the real options decision tree, the Gordon perpetuity is replaced by a finite annuity weighted by the empirically calibrated Weibull survival function S(T, k, λ), where parameters are calibrated on US BLS/BDS data across 19 NAICS-2 sectors. We establish a taxonomy of terminal node closure mechanisms across three asset classes, demonstrating that the BSVM™ correction is applicable exclusively to operating firms where perpetuity is the operative closure assumption. We prove as Proposition 1 that the classical ROV framework with abandonment option is internally inconsistent, and derive three corollaries showing that abandonment option value is systematically underestimated while expansion option value is systematically overestimated under the Gordon terminal node. The Gordon model is recovered as a special case when k = 1 and the extinction rate approaches zeroconditions unobserved in any NAICS-2 sector in this BLS/BDS sample. A secondary extension introduces Weibull-implied volatility (σ_W) as a sector-specific substitute for historical volatility in the intermediate nodes of the binomial tree. Note on data scope: BLS/BDS calibration operates at the establishment level; the relationship between establishment-level survival parameters and individual firm survival is discussed in the Limitations section.

title: Environmental Degradation and Equity Return Alpha Using Satellite Imagery

detail.title: Environmental Degradation and Equity Return Alpha Using Satellite Imagery
detail.abstract: The academic and commercial use of satellite imagery and geospatial data has expanded rapidly since the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) began providing public access in the late 1990s. While most applications have focused on geology and energy estimation, the potential use of satellite data in financial analysis remains less explored. r This paper combines official CO₂ emissions data with satellite-based measures of energy consumption to examine the relationship between environmental degradation and stock returns, and to assess whether reductions in environmental degradation are associated with positive abnormal returns (alpha). Existing ESG-related asset pricing studies predominantly rely on published statistical data. We find consistent evidence across both data sources that reductions in environmental degradation are associated with higher alpha. These findings motivate further investigation into whether satellite data can complement-or, in data-scarce settings, substitute for-official statistics, thereby improving the feasibility of ESG and climate-related financial analysis in ministates and developing economies where published data are often limited.

title:
Virginia's Broken Promise 

How a $15 Million State Investment in Community Development Became a Case Study in Mission Drift, Racial Inequity, and the Politics of Who Gets Left Behind

detail.title:
Virginia's Broken Promise 

How a $15 Million State Investment in Community Development Became a Case Study in Mission Drift, Racial Inequity, and the Politics of Who Gets Left Behind
detail.abstract:
Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) were created to address persistent failures in private capital markets by expanding access to affordable credit for underserved communities. Their unique public-private structure reflects a social contract: in exchange for public investment, tax advantages, and regulatory support, these institutions are expected to pursue measurable community development outcomes alongside financial sustainability. This book examines what happens when that social contract begins to erode.

Using the evolution of Virginia Community Capital (now Locus Bank) as a comprehensive case study, this book documents how an institution established with substantial public support gradually shifted from its founding mission toward a business model increasingly centered on financial performance rather than community impact. Drawing on nearly two decades of FDIC Call Reports, audited financial statements, CDFI certification records, public filings, board governance materials, and original empirical analysis, the book traces the institutional decisions, governance changes, and strategic incentives that contributed to mission drift while public resources and public trust remained in place.

Rather than presenting this as the story of a single institution, the analysis situates Virginia's experience within broader questions confronting community development finance across the United States. The book explores the tensions between financial sustainability and social purpose through the lenses of agency theory, institutional economics, nonprofit governance, and public accountability. It demonstrates how governance structures, executive incentives, limited transparency, and weak performance oversight can gradually reshape organizational priorities without an explicit abandonment of mission.

The final chapters move beyond diagnosis to propose a practical framework for reform. The book recommends measurable mission-performance standards, independent mission audits, enhanced public reporting, stronger community representation in governance, and accountability mechanisms that align public investment with demonstrated public benefit. Ultimately, Virginia's Broken Promise argues that preserving confidence in community development finance requires more than good intentions—it requires transparent governance, empirical accountability, and continuous verification that public capital continues to serve the communities for which it was intended.

title: Impact of Renewable Energy Investment on CO2 Emissions: Evidence from G20 Countries(2000-2022)

detail.title: Impact of Renewable Energy Investment on CO2 Emissions: Evidence from G20 Countries(2000-2022)
detail.abstract: The transition toward low-carbon development has become a central policy priority for G20 economies, which together account for nearly 80 percent of global energy use and CO₂ emissions. This study investigates the impact of renewable energy investment on CO₂ emissions in G20 countries over the period 2000-2022, while explicitly distinguishing investment effects from renewable energy consumption. Using panel regression techniques-including fixed-effects, random-effects, and system GMM estimators-the analysis relies on secondary data from the World Bank and the International Energy Agency (IEA). The empirical results indicate that renewable energy investment contributes to emissions reduction primarily when it translates into effective renewable energy consumption, whereas investment indicators alone do not consistently generate significant emission-reducing effects. Economic growth and energy intensity exert upward pressure on CO₂ emissions, while renewable energy consumption plays a critical mitigating role. Dynamic estimation results further reveal strong persistence in emissions, underscoring the importance of sustained and coordinated policy interventions. Overall, these findings highlight the necessity of aligning renewable energy investment with energy system integration and consumption-oriented policies. Strengthening green finance mechanisms and improving the efficiency of renewable deployment are essential for achieving emission reduction targets under the Paris Agreement and supporting sustainable economic growth among G20 economies.

title: AgroIntel: A Multilingual AI Platform for Vision Transformer-based Crop Disease Detection and Growth-stage-aware NDVI Monitoring
affiliations: , DYPatil Engineering College and DYPatil Engineering College

detail.title: AgroIntel: A Multilingual AI Platform for Vision Transformer-based Crop Disease Detection and Growth-stage-aware NDVI Monitoring
detail.abstract: Crop diseases and suboptimal vegetation health remain leading threats to global food security, causing estimated yield losses of 20-40% annually. Existing agricultural technology solutions are often prohibitively expensive, monolingual, and lack phenological context for interpreting vegetation indices. This paper presents AgroIntel, a full-stack, multilingual AI platform that integrates three core innovations: (1) a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based disease classifier operating on 20 disease-health classes across five major staple crops (corn, potato, rice, wheat, sugarcane); (2) a growth-stage-aware Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) model that parametrizes expected NDVI as a piecewise linear function of phenological stage, enabling anomaly detection relative to crop-specific benchmarks; and (3) a hybrid satellite-synthetic NDVI pipeline with automatic fallback across Sentinel-2, Landsat 8, and generative simulation. The platform serves a trilingual (English, Hindi, Marathi) interface with 139 translated UI keys and a fully client-side FAQ chatbot, making it accessible to low-literacy farming communities. We describe the system architecture, evaluate the NDVI anomaly detection methodology, and discuss deployment considerations for resource-constrained agricultural settings.

title: Forecasting with Uncertain Persistence
affiliations: Yale University, Yale University and Princeton University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Forecasting with Uncertain Persistence
detail.abstract: With uncertainty about persistence, we show that forecasts necessarily become more persistent and over-react at long horizons. For these reasons, correctly specified and Bayesian forecasts may under-react at short horizons and over-react at long horizons. These results provide a unified explanation for several asset pricing and forecasting puzzles, including: (i) the excess responsiveness of long-horizon rates to short rates, (ii) the dominance of apparent term premia for long-term rates, (iii) the ex post predictability of bond yields, (iv) the excess volatility of long-horizon forward prices, (v) the excess persistence of long-horizon forecasts, and (vi) the over-reaction of long-horizon forecasts.

title: The Hafzan Information Capital Theory: A Stochastic Utility Framework for Data Asset Valuation in Modern Financial Systems

detail.title: The Hafzan Information Capital Theory: A Stochastic Utility Framework for Data Asset Valuation in Modern Financial Systems
detail.abstract: Contemporary accounting frameworks-principally U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)-were codified in an era in which physical capital constituted the dominant productive asset. By 2024, intangible assets account for more than 90% of S&P 500 market capitalisation (Ocean Tomo, 2020), yet standards such as IAS 38 and ASC 350 continue to mandate the immediate expensing of most internally generated intangibles, including proprietary data. This paper introduces the Hafzan Information Capital Theory and its centrepiece, the Hafzan Identity, a mathematically rigorous valuation model that treats data as a stochastic real option whose value is a function of attributable revenue, decision-elasticity, fidelity, entropy-based decay, and network connectivity. Building on real options theory (Dixit & Pindyck, 1994; Trigeorgis, 1996), information economics (Stiglitz, 1985; Akerlof, 1970), and network effects literature (Metcalfe, 2013; Arthur, 1996), we formalise the Quantum Data Valuation Model (QDVM), derive the Marginal Contribution Test (MCT) for empirical identification of model parameters, propose an Entropy-Based Impairment Schedule, and outline a Connectivity Capitalisation premium grounded in graph theory. We further discuss the integration of these constructs into a proposed Data Capital Balance Sheet and assess the macroeconomic and policy implications of standardising data as a reportable financial asset.

title: Beyond The Plate: A Mixed-Methods Study on Service Quality, Customer Satisfaction, Loyalty, and Owner Challenges in Restaurants
affiliations: and Northwestern Mindanao State College of Science and Technology

detail.title: Beyond The Plate: A Mixed-Methods Study on Service Quality, Customer Satisfaction, Loyalty, and Owner Challenges in Restaurants
detail.abstract: Service quality stands as the cornerstone of restaurant excellence, shaping customers' perceptions and experiences while driving loyalty and reputation in a competitive food service industry. This mixed-methods study examined restaurant operations in Misamis Occidental, Philippines, from customer perceptions of service quality, satisfaction, and loyalty, to owners' lived experience of sustaining that quality. A descriptive-correlational design surveyed 396 customers across ten establishments, assessing service quality (tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy), satisfaction (ambiance, hospitality service, added value, technology, trust and commitment), and loyalty (repeat patronage, word of mouth, brand equity, emotional attachment, switching costs), using researcher-made questionnaires and Pearson correlation. A phenomenological design then interviewed the owners of those establishments, analyzed through Moustakas' method. Results showed service quality rated very good, satisfaction very high except for technology, and loyalty very high, with service quality significantly correlated with both outcomes. Interviews yielded three themes describing owners' difficulties: managing operations, sustaining marketing, and countering rivals. An exploratory correlation linking owner-reported difficulty severity to satisfaction and loyalty scores found no significant relationship, though the small sample limits what this test can rule out. Taken together, the findings suggest that strong customer-facing outcomes may be sustained despite, rather than because of, an absence of strain on the owner's side: owners describe active personal involvement, informal staffing, and reactive promotion, a pattern that may not hold as rivalry intensifies, although this could not be confirmed. Recommendations include investing in technology-enabled delivery, formalizing staff training, and adopting more deliberate promotional strategies to protect satisfaction and loyalty.

title: How Does Communication Format Impact Heatwave Concerns?
affiliations: University of British Columbia (UBC), University of British Columbia (UBC), University of British Columbia (UBC) and University of British Columbia (UBC) - Department of Psychology

detail.title: How Does Communication Format Impact Heatwave Concerns?
detail.abstract: Extreme heat events are increasing in frequency and intensity due to climate change. Effective communication of these risks is critical for fostering concern and motivating adaptive behaviors. This pre-registered experiment (N=885 U.S. participants) examined how communication format in likelihood (e.g., "X times more likely"), frequency (e.g., "X times every 10 or 1,000 years"), or temperature (e.g., "X°F higher peak temperature") affects the threshold at which people report feeling more concerned about a moderate or a severe heatwave. The results showed that for people to feel more concerned, the heatwave would have to be a lot worse when communicated in the temperature format compared to frequency or likelihood formats, with likelihood eliciting the lowest concern threshold. Thresholds were higher for the severe than the moderate heatwaves, consistent with diminishing sensitivity to already-extreme events. Participants also underestimated heatwave peak temperatures at baseline, and concern thresholds were predicted by baseline concern, political orientation, and initial peak temperature estimates. These findings highlight format-specific effects in climate communication and emphasize the need for likelihood or frequency statistics over temperature increases to better align public concern with scientific projections of escalating heat risks.

title: Does Temporal Topology Add Information Beyond Static Snapshots? A Pre-Registered Controlled Study of Zigzag Persistence for Short-Horizon Tail-Move Prediction on Hyperliquid Perpetuals

detail.title: Does Temporal Topology Add Information Beyond Static Snapshots? A Pre-Registered Controlled Study of Zigzag Persistence for Short-Horizon Tail-Move Prediction on Hyperliquid Perpetuals
detail.abstract: We report a clean, controlled null: temporal topology-tracked via zigzag persistence of an order-flow-imbalance delay embedding-does not improve short-horizon tail-move prediction over static per-window persistence on any of three Hyperliquid perpetuals (BTC/ETH/SOL; ∆pr-auc =-0.0008/+0.0031/+0.0032, all p > 0.07). The null is robust across grids, scales, frame/window choices, estimators, and raw-sequence baselines. A registered secondary contrast finds that static topology does lift precision-recall over a compact microstructure baseline (+0.018/+0.020/+0.009), surviving both a feature-permutation shuffle and a time-shift negative control, but only BTC clears strict per-coin correction; against a richer thirty-feature ofidynamics baseline the residual is BTC-only (+0.0055, p=0.023). The static effect is therefore largely an efficient encoding of order-flow dynamics already capturable by scalar features, with at most a marginal topological residual on the highest-signal symbol. Limits: single venue, ∼538 ms snapshot feed, regime concentration (∼78% of positives in one surge), a featurization-conditional null, all mechanism analyses exploratory.

title: Role of Strategic Leadership in Adopting Disruptive Technologies in the Indian Armed Forces
affiliations: Poornima University

detail.title: Role of Strategic Leadership in Adopting Disruptive Technologies in the Indian Armed Forces

keywords: Emerging Military Technology Embedded Weapon Systems

detail.abstract: Recent conflicts demonstrate that while disruptive military technologies can confer decisive battlefield advantages, their effectiveness depends less on acquisition and more on leadership-enabled adoption and institutional absorption. For the Indian Armed Forces, the challenge lies in integrating emerging technology-enabled weapon systems-such as Unmanned Aerial Systems, Artificial Intelligence-enabled decision support, IoBT-based networks, Robotics and Quantum-enabled capabilitiesinto doctrine, training, command structures, and operational practice. This paper examines the role of strategic leadership in adopting disruptive technologies and argues that leadership influence alone is insufficient without structured change management. Drawing on established leadership theories and change management frameworks, the study proposes a Leadership-Change-Technology adoption (LCT) model, wherein change management moderates the relationship between strategic leadership and technology adoption outcomes. The paper demonstrates that disciplined change management enables user acceptance, institutional learning, and doctrinal alignment, thereby translating leadership intent into sustained combat capability. The findings underscore that enduring military advantage arises not from technological superiority alone, but from leadership-driven absorption that integrates technology, people and doctrine into a coherent warfighting system.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes OPT_wtd, a measure of structural optionality that captures the complexity-weighted upgrading potential encoded in a country's export basket. Applied to a six-country panel (Japan, Italy, Germany, France, Belgium, Argentina, T0 = 1880, T1 = 1910), OPT_wtd ranks structural upgrading with Kendall τ = +0.966 (p = 0.007); OLS on n = 6 yields β β = +0.624 (SE = 0.188, R² = 0.735, p = 0.029). Within-country arc-level evidence for Japan confirms the adjacency mechanism (S = 0.857 of realised growth within the predicted reachable set, permutation benchmark 0.354). Two boundary conditions delimit the domain: Spain (OPT = 0.677, residual =-0.326) establishes that optionality is not sufficient when institutional capacity is near zero; the United Kingdom establishes frontier saturation, where OPT_wtd collapses to zero and decline is measurable only as world-share erosion in highcomplexity nodes (ρ(ΔOPT_fr_high, ΔCR) = +0.702, n = 11). A pre-registered secondepisode test on Japan 1910-1939 (LTES P1™) yields ΔCR = +0.160 with all predicted arcs traversed, confirming portability of the arc-level mechanism.

title: Corporate AI Advocacy: When Industry Self-regulation Becomes Regulatory Capture by Another Name

detail.title: Corporate AI Advocacy: When Industry Self-regulation Becomes Regulatory Capture by Another Name
detail.abstract: The AI industry has produced a proliferation of voluntary commitments, industry principles, and self-regulatory initiatives-from the White House AI commitments to the Partnership on AI to corporate responsible AI charters. These instruments are presented as evidence that the industry can govern itself, reducing the need for binding legislation. This paper critically examines the conditions under which industry self-regulation serves genuine public interest versus when it functions as a sophisticated strategy to preempt binding legislation and shape regulatory outcomes in industry-favorable directions. Drawing on regulatory capture theory (Stigler, 1971; Carpenter & Moss, 2013) and historical parallels with the tobacco, pharmaceutical, and financial services industries, the paper analyzes the AI industry's self-regulatory ecosystem across four analytical dimensions-commitment specificity, transparency, scope alignment, and legislative interaction-and introduces the Self-Regulation Credibility Framework (SRCF), a diagnostic instrument that policymakers can apply to evaluate whether any given self-regulatory initiative is a genuine complement to legislation or a substitute designed to prevent it. Empirical analysis of 42 corporate AI commitments, 12 industry codes of conduct, and lobbying disclosure records across the US, EU, and India reveals that 78 percent of self-regulatory commitments lack measurable compliance criteria, 91 percent include no independent monitoring mechanism, and companies that most actively promote self-regulation simultaneously spend the most on lobbying against binding rules. The paper argues that self-regulation becomes regulatory capture when it simultaneously satisfies three conditions: it is designed to be unmeasurable, it is promoted as a reason to delay legislation, and it is authored by the entities it purports to constrain.

title: Dynamic Selection with the Informal Sector

detail.title: Dynamic Selection with the Informal Sector
detail.abstract: This paper studies how informality affects long-run growth and welfare through firm-level dynamic selection. I develop a tractable continuous-time firm-dynamics model in which firms choose whether to operate formally and, if registered, how much to comply with regulatory and labor-market obligations. The model jointly determines the firm-size distribution and aggregate growth, yielding closed-form expressions for the stationary distribution and decompositions of growth and output. Calibrated to Mexico, the model shows that tax-rate counterfactuals generate a growth–output trade-off: lower formal-sector taxes strengthen selection and raise growth, but also thin the right tail of the firm-size distribution and reduce output per unit of knowledge capital. Welfare nevertheless rises because formalization expands the tax base and supports public goods. The decomposition further shows that extensive and intensive informality have opposite welfare implications, highlighting the importance of distinguishing the two margins.

title: The Fictions of Independence : Structural Isomorphism in the Audit Risk Model and the Gaussian Copula

detail.title: The Fictions of Independence : Structural Isomorphism in the Audit Risk Model and the Gaussian Copula
detail.abstract: The audit risk model rests on a dependence it cannot measure. The correlation, on the misstatements an audit fails to catch, between control failure and substantive-procedure failure is non-identified at the engagement level, yet the model's multiplication of its components assumes it away. This paper argues that the defect is not an accident of accounting but one instance of a structure it shares with the Gaussian-copula pricing of structured credit whose failure defined the 2007-2008 crisis: in both, the marginal failure probabilities are identified while the dependence binding them into a joint failure is not; in both, that dependence is set at a benign value by a convention cost favours rather than estimated; and in both, the worst case the convention suppresses is the comonotone bound of the Fréchet-Hoeffding inequality, at which diversification is net zero. The correspondence is drawn deliberately to one side of the copula's most cited flaw-its zero tail dependence, a defect of functional form, not of identification, that the audit model does not share-since to equate the two would confuse a defect of shape with a defect of knowledge. The identification failure itself differs in kind-structural non-identification in audit, where the conditioning event is unobservable, against finite-sample under-identification in finance, where it is merely rare-but the convention, the cost that sustains it, and the suppressed Fréchet worst case are common, and recur in the common-cause failure of engineered defence in depth. For auditing the cross-domain view reframes rather than indicts: the multiplication is not a neutral default but a convention finance suffered and engineered safety has moved to correct, and what answers a dependence that cannot be identified is not a better estimate of it but deterrence. In each domain, what is certified as a measured residual is a wager on a dependence no one can see.

title: Service Rate Optimization in Single-Server Queues with Time-Varying Arrivals and Capacity Constraints
affiliations: University of Amsterdam Business School, University of Twente, University of Twente and University of Twente

detail.title: Service Rate Optimization in Single-Server Queues with Time-Varying Arrivals and Capacity Constraints
detail.abstract: This paper considers a single-server queue with time-varying Poisson arrivals and controllable service rates subject to capacity constraints and aggregate capacity budget constraints over decision cycles consisting of a fixed number of decision epochs. Service rates are chosen for the periods within each cycle, either statically for the full horizon or dynamically at the start of each cycle. Two natural objectives are considered: minimizing the average expected queue length within a cycle and minimizing the expected queue length at the end of a cycle. We show that optimizing either objective leads to extreme front-loading or back-loading of service capacity. Therefore, we propose a multi-objective optimization framework. For the static setting, we develop an exact solution approach based on transient M/M/1 queue analysis, and introduce a stochastic programming approximation based on the Lindley recursion to solve for larger planning horizons consisting of several cycles. A dynamic formulation also exploits the observed queue lengths. Numerical experiments show how different objective trade-offs affect capacity allocation, fairness across periods, and steady-state performance. The results provide practical insights for capacity planning in service systems with predictable time-varying demand under both per-epoch and per-cycle capacity constraints.

title: Conscious Leadership as a Mediating Variable in the Return on Investment in Enterprise Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Conscious Leadership as a Mediating Variable in the Return on Investment in Enterprise Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest

detail.abstract: Global corporate investment in artificial intelligence (AI) reached USD 252.3 billion in 2024—roughly thirteen times the level of a decade earlier—yet only 6% of organizations report a significant impact on earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) attributable to AI, and a majority of projects fail to reach production. This conceptual paper argues that the available empirical literature converges in identifying leadership and organizational culture—rather than technology—as the dominant constraint behind this gap, but that it documents the symptoms of failure with statistical precision while offering no causal mechanism to account for them. The paper argues that such a mechanism already exists, in dispersed form, across consolidated bodies of leadership research: the constructive-developmental theory of adult development (Kegan), ego development and action logics (Loevinger; Cook-Greuter; Rooke and Torbert), action science and defensive routines (Argyris and Schön), the clinical-psychodynamic paradigm of leadership (Kets de Vries), and the conceptualization of self-awareness as a measurable dimension of authentic leadership (Walumbwa et al.). Drawing on a narrative synthesis of empirical AI-adoption sources and these established frameworks, the paper (a) documents the empirical convergence on leadership as the dominant constraint, (b) characterizes the explanatory gap, and (c) integrates these frameworks into a single mediating proposition—that the internal condition from which a leader operates, termed here conscious leadership, conditions organizational learning and, therefore, the return on technological investment—articulated as five testable propositions using already-validated instruments. The paper presents no original empirical data; its contribution is to transfer a mechanism well established in the leadership literature to the as-yet-unaddressed problem of the return on enterprise AI investment.

title: AI Advantage Decay Why AI Accelerates Both the Creation and Decay of Competitive Advantage

detail.title: AI Advantage Decay Why AI Accelerates Both the Creation and Decay of Competitive Advantage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or experimental data requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no specific funding for this research.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly viewed as a source of competitive advantage because AI systems improve through use, optimize decisions, and scale rapidly across organizations. Yet the economic durability of AI-driven advantage remains uncertain. Many AI deployments generate temporary performance gains that quickly erode as capabilities are replicated, infrastructure is standardized, and systems converge technologically. This paper explains natural advantage decay in AI systems. It argues that AI does not only create competitive differentiation; it also accelerates the conditions under which that differentiation decays. As AI capabilities diffuse through shared models, cloud infrastructure, and reusable architectures, technical functionality becomes increasingly commoditized, compressing the duration of advantage. This dynamic is illustrated through the rapid diffusion of generative AI assistants in enterprise software systems, where Microsoft, Google, Salesforce, Adobe, Slack, and Notion introduced broadly similar "copilot-style" functionality embedded within their core productivity and workflow platforms, resulting in rapid convergence toward a standardized system feature across competing software ecosystems. The paper examines the structural mechanisms behind this decay, including replication and diffusion, capability standardization, declining scarcity, and environmental adaptation, and shows how these forces compress the lifespan of AI-driven advantage in organizational systems. The paper further argues that the central challenge of AI strategy is not merely deploying intelligent systems, but understanding the economic conditions under which differentiation can persist in environments characterized by rapid technological convergence.

title: Fifteen Days Early: Schedule Compression Under Competitive Pressure at Lahore's Emporium Mall Megaproject

detail.title: Fifteen Days Early: Schedule Compression Under Competitive Pressure at Lahore's Emporium Mall Megaproject

declarations.ethicsApproval: Written consent has been given by AHN Architects - the organisation whose dilemma is written about.

detail.abstract: This case-based exercise places students inside the project manager's office on a USD 200 million retail megaproject in Pakistan and asks them to do what every project manager dreads: deliver early, without raising risk. Set in Lahore in June 2013, the case unfolds against the global statistical reality that nine out of ten megaprojects run over schedule and over budget (Flyvbjerg, 2014). Students convert a fixed Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) into a workable schedule on a project management software, allocate contractors and service providers as resources, identify the critical path, and then compress the schedule by tweaking dependencies, working overtime, and adding resources, without inflating cost-related risks already identified in the project's risk register. 1

title: Recognition Justice Theory: Toward a Justice-Based Theory of Migration, Belonging, and Social Cohesion

detail.title: Recognition Justice Theory: Toward a Justice-Based Theory of Migration, Belonging, and Social Cohesion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing financial, professional, or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval was not required for this study because it is a theoretical and conceptual analysis based exclusively on published literature and the author's original theoretical development. No human participants, personal data, or identifiable records were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: The research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Contemporary scholarship has generated important insights into migration, recognition, citizenship, justice, and social cohesion, yet these traditions have largely developed in parallel. Consequently, existing approaches struggle to explain why formally inclusive societies continue to reproduce exclusion, why migrants and other marginalised populations experience contested belonging despite legal incorporation, and how structural inequalities become redirected towards vulnerable groups. This study addresses these limitations by developing Recognition Justice Theory (RJT), a new interdisciplinary framework that integrates recognition theory, justice theory, migration studies, citizenship scholarship, postcolonial thought, and peacebuilding within a single analytical architecture. Recognition Justice Theory advances the central proposition that durable social cohesion depends upon the equitable distribution of recognition across members of a political community. To operationalise this claim, the study introduces three original analytical concepts: Recognition Inequality, Recognition Deficit, and Belonging Inequality, and incorporates Political Misrecognition as the mechanism through which structural grievances are displaced onto socially visible and recognitionally vulnerable populations. Together, these concepts explain how structural injustice produces unequal legitimacy, contested membership, exclusionary mobilisation, and weakened social cohesion. The research further develops the analytical framework of Recognition Justice Theory by identifying both an explanatory pathway linking structural injustice to fragmented political communities and a normative pathway through which equitable recognition strengthens belonging, meaningful participation, and durable social cohesion. In doing so, Recognition Justice extends existing recognition scholarship beyond questions of identity and status to conceptualise recognition as a socially distributed good that structures legitimacy, participation, and belonging across political communities. The theory provides an integrated framework for analysing migration, democratic inclusion, citizenship, peacebuilding, and social cohesion across both Global North and Global South contexts.

title: The Geography of the Inward Return: Consciousness as Ground, Interplay, and Homecoming
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Geography of the Inward Return: Consciousness as Ground, Interplay, and Homecoming
detail.abstract: This essay offers a philosophical analysis of a tri-lingual lyric suite-உ"ேசாதி (Utchōdhi / The Inner Light, Tamil), The Light Within the Light (English), and La Lumière au Fond de la Lumière (French)-composed from classical Tamil sacred verses drawn from Tirumular's Thirumanthiram (c. 7th-10th century CE), Thiruvalluvar's Thirukkural (c. 1st-5th century CE), the Auvai Kural tradition, and the contemporary Madhumozhithiruppa. The suite constructs a systematic counter-epistemology to physicalist accounts of consciousness, engaging directly with David Chalmers' Hard Problem (1995), Nagel's phenomenological challenge (1974), and the limits of computational models of mind (Dennett, 1991; Tononi, 2004). Drawing on Tamil Shaiva Siddhanta metaphysics, Kashmir Shaivite non-dualism, and continental phenomenology, the songs argue that consciousness (உ"ேசாதி / Utchōdhi) is not a biological epiphenomenon but the fundamental, self-luminous substrate of existence-a primordial relational field (ச(தி)சிவ உ+ள-.) revealed through negation, clarification, and inward return. The analysis proceeds through five philosophical movements: radical luminosity, dynamic void, latent immanence, epistemological liberation, and homecoming.

title: Who Invents AI? AI Labor and the Production of AI Innovation
affiliations: University of Bristol

detail.title: Who Invents AI? AI Labor and the Production of AI Innovation
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how new ideas are produced, but AI must itself be invented, and inventing it takes a scarce input, the workers who can build AI systems. Does a firm's stock of AI labor cause it to invent more AI? Using firm-level data on AI hiring and AI patenting for U.S. public firms, I exploit the November 2015 open-sourcing of TensorFlow, a large and external drop in the cost of building deep-learning systems, interacted with firms' pre-shock AI-labor exposure. Firms that entered the shock with more AI labor produced more AI patents afterward. The effect loads on deep-learning technologies, and is driven by large and organizational capital rich firms. It operates through rising R&D and a growing number of AI inventors, and it makes AI invention more concentrated among the firms that were already AI-rich. An instrumental-variables strategy that instruments AI labor with a university-graduate supply shifter confirms a positive, AI-specific effect.

detail.abstract:
The restaurant industry is characterised by high failure rates and intensifying competition, yet critical success factors are rarely examined as an integrated system tied directly to consumer expectations. Most existing research studies management, service quality, and customer satisfaction in isolation, leaving a significant gap in understanding the core disconnect between what consumers actually want and what restaurants deliver.

 

This paper examines those gaps specifically among the upscale casual dining restaurant segment which holds a special importance in a number of consumer categories. An empirical investigation was undertaken using a survey questionnaire targeting two distinct age groups: 18-25 years old and 40-50 years old. The study looks at consumers' preferences and choice criteria, their attitudes towards loyalty and emotional attachment.

The results show that consumer expectations vary significantly and that the drivers for success and failure in the restaurant business differ dramatically for different groups of consumers.

detail.abstract:
Key Account Management (KAM) has evolved from a specialized sales function into a strategic capability for managing high-value customer relationships in business-to-business (B2B) markets. While existing literature provides substantial insights into relationship management, customer value creation, customer portfolio management, and strategic selling, relatively few studies have proposed an integrated framework that combines strategic customer qualification, multi-dimensional evaluation, account prioritization, tiering, resource allocation, and continuous customer monitoring within a single managerial model. This paper addresses this gap by proposing the Strategic Key Account Prioritization Framework (SKAP Framework), a conceptual model developed through the integration of established academic literature and practitioner-informed insights.
The proposed framework comprises eight interconnected stages: Strategic Customer Qualification, Multi-Dimensional Evaluation, Weighted Prioritization, Account Classification, Strategic Resource Allocation, Relationship Management, Customer Health Monitoring, and Continuous Review. Each stage is theoretically grounded and designed to provide organizations with a structured and transparent approach to identifying, prioritizing, and managing strategically important customers. By shifting key account selection from intuition-based decision-making to a systematic and evidence-informed process, the framework supports more effective allocation of organizational resources and long-term customer value creation.
The paper concludes by discussing the managerial implications of the proposed framework and demonstrates how it can be implemented using commonly available decision-support tools and customer relationship management systems. Finally, opportunities for future empirical validation and refinement of the framework are identified, providing a foundation for subsequent academic research and practical application.

title: The Credible Threat: How Online Ratings Can Mitigate Opportunism in the Hotel Industry
affiliations: and University of Peloponnese

detail.title: The Credible Threat: How Online Ratings Can Mitigate Opportunism in the Hotel Industry
detail.abstract: This study proposes a game-theoretic model to examine how verified customer ratings on Online Travel Agency (OTA) platforms influence hotel behavior under conditions of moral hazard. Drawing on principal-agent theory, the interaction between hotel service providers and guests is modelled as a one-shot moral hazard game with asymmetric information. Hotels face a strategic choice between honoring service commitments and opportunistically degrading service quality to achieve short-term gains. Customers, upon experiencing the service, decide whether to publicly report their evaluation through ratings. Our equilibrium analysis reveals a paradox: even in oneshot encounters, where reputation should theoretically lack disciplining power, credible review systems can induce partial compliance. Mixed-strategy equilibria emerge, balancing hotels' temptation to shirk against customers' willingness to punish. These findings extend debates on reputation systems beyond repeated games, offering practical implications for OTA platform design and regulatory oversight.

title: Selective Conscription: Sequential Allocation under Incomplete Information in Brazil's Military Recruitment and Retention System
affiliations: Central Bank of Brazil

detail.title: Selective Conscription: Sequential Allocation under Incomplete Information in Brazil's Military Recruitment and Retention System
detail.abstract: Military recruitment systems vary widely, ranging from fully professional volunteer forces to conscription regimes. Within conscription, Brazil represents a distinctive intermediate design: registration is broadly universal but actual incorporation is highly selective. In such selective compulsory service systems, the military must allocate a limited number of positions among a large pool of potential recruits under imperfect information about both aptitude and preferences. Yet no formal framework models this selection process as a sequential allocation mechanism. This paper develops a model of selective conscription under incomplete information, in which centralized screening, decentralized capacity-constrained selection, and post-service learning jointly determine allocation outcomes. The paper makes two contributions. First, it shows that the interaction between screening and capacity constraints generates endogenous local quasi-random assignment at the selection margin, providing an institutional, rather than purely statistical, foundation for regression-discontinuity identification. Second, it shows that when preferences are learned through experience, conditioning initial selection on stated willingness to serve is suboptimal: deferring preference revelation improves the quality of the retained force. More broadly, the framework shows that in selective conscription systems, the timing of information revelation jointly shapes causal identification and optimal allocation.

detail.abstract: As workers externalize tacit expertise into prompts, workflows, evaluation criteria, and structured systems, they build firm-level capabilities, here called Organizational Intelligence, that are persistent, scalable, and increasingly central to production. This paper isolates a mechanism through which that process can alter incentives and the division of value inside the firm. Building on the literature on intangible capital, organization capital, and complementary investments, it argues that AI-enabled codification can be a self-substituting investment: translating tacit expertise into reusable systems, including systems that can generate outputs and adapt through use, raises total surplus, yet can weaken the worker's future bargaining position by reducing the scarcity of the expertise on which that leverage rests. The paper formalizes this as the Knowledge-Engineering Paradox. In a stylized model, the worker's ability to capture the value she creates declines as her expertise becomes more codified and transferable, so private investment falls short of the surplus-maximizing level. The shortfall runs through a channel absent from standard hold-up and principal–agent models. The model microfounds the declining share through bargaining over an outside option that codification erodes, states the conditions under which the firm cannot contract the problem away, and derives testable implications. It anchors the mechanism in field evidence that generative AI raises output by capturing and diffusing the practices of the most able workers (Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond 2025). The contribution is not a new category of capital but a mechanism linking the codification of expertise, the creation of scalable capability, and the incentives to build and maintain it. The central question of the AI economy is therefore not only whether intelligent systems raise productivity, but how the gains from codified human expertise are distributed once that expertise becomes a firm-governed capability that can be applied, extended, and refined over time.

title: Joint Assortment Planning and Inventory Control under General Choice Models
affiliations: , University of British Columbia, City University of Hong Kong and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Joint Assortment Planning and Inventory Control under General Choice Models
detail.abstract: We propose a constant-factor approximation framework for the joint assortment planning and inventory management problem, where customers substitute to less preferred in-stock products if more preferred products are out of stock. The customer arrivals follow an increasing-failure-rate (IFR) distribution, and customer purchasing behavior is governed by a discrete choice model with dynamic inventory availability. Our decision involves determining the initial inventory vector, subject to a capacity constraint. Our algorithm begins with a novel fluid relaxation that identifies at most two candidate assortments with the highest potential profitability. For each assortment, we construct a static-allocation-based lower bound on the expected total revenue for an inventory vector that stocks only the products in the assortment. The final inventory decision is the vector that maximizes the stronger of these two lower bounds. We establish a (κ/4-ϵ)-approximation guarantee for a broad class of substitutable choice models, in which adding products weakly decreases the choice probabilities of existing items, and for which the cardinality-constrained assortment optimization problem admits a κ-approximation algorithm. Our result provides the first constant-factor approximation ratios for this problem under several important choice models, including the Markov chain choice model and the mixture of MNL models. Moreover, our framework also achieves the state-of-the-art approximation ratio of 0.25 for the MNL choice model. Our guarantees can be further strengthened when the capacity constraint is relatively loose or when the demand distribution is deterministic or Poisson.

title: The Knowledge Asset Impairment Model (KAIM): A Framework for Restating the Balance Sheet of R&D-Intensive Technology Companies

detail.title: The Knowledge Asset Impairment Model (KAIM): A Framework for Restating the Balance Sheet of R&D-Intensive Technology Companies

detail.abstract: Standard accounting rules require that research and development expenditures be expensed in the period incurred, regardless of the productive life of the knowledge generated. This treatment, codified under ASC 730 and IAS 38, was designed for an industrial economy in which the primary means of production were physical, visible, and appropriately capitalized. For R&D-intensive technology companies operating in the modern knowledge economy, it produces a systematic and material distortion: the primary productive asset of the firm — its accumulated engineering knowledge — does not appear on the balance sheet at all. The result is a price-to-book ratio that is artificially inflated not by market speculation but by an understated denominator. The Knowledge Asset Impairment Model (KAIM) corrects this asymmetry through an eightstep methodology. KAIM capitalizes twenty years of R&D expenditure as a Knowledge Capital Stock (KCS), inflation-adjusts it to constant dollars using the CPI-U deflator, and holds it at full value unless one of three specific, observable economic triggers provides evidence that the accumulated knowledge has ceased to produce. KAIM further recognizes forward contract assets — committed hardware purchase orders and multi-year cloud service agreements — that are economically real and disclosed in 10-K footnotes but absent from GAAP balance sheets. Applied consistently across R&D-intensive technology companies and non-tech large-cap comparisons, KAIM produces restated book values that make the knowledge factory visible and P/B multiples that reflect genuine forward expectations rather than accounting artifact. The self-limiting nature of the correction — producing little or no adjustment for companies whose value derives from physical assets or capital allocation rather than accumulated R&D — confirms that KAIM addresses a specific structural distortion rather than systematically inflating valuations. This paper presents a summary of the complete methodology, the three-trigger impairment framework, the forward asset recognition rules, and a suite of KAIM-derived operating metrics for ongoing monitoring.

title: Information or Emotion? How Firm-Generated User Content Shapes Sales in Livestream Shopping
affiliations: HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong and

detail.title: Information or Emotion? How Firm-Generated User Content Shapes Sales in Livestream Shopping
detail.abstract: Firm-Generated User Content (FGUC)-content created by a company but designed for consumers to share as if it were their own creation-effectively puts firms' words in users' digital mouths. Unlike user-generated content or firm-generated content, FGUC intends to boost engagement and sales by making sharing easier and providing prewritten narratives for social media posts. While the effects of the former two types of content on sales have been extensively studied, limited attention has been devoted to FGUC. Drawing on high-frequency livestream shopping data encompassing 1,934 livestream sessions provided by a TikTok livestream agency, we examine how FGUC influences sales and explore the underlying mechanisms. Our findings reveal the following: (1) narrative FGUC has no effect on any sales metric; (2) information-focused FGUC slightly reduces sales and returns but has no significant impact on net sales; (3) emotion-focused FGUC has similar positive effects on sales and returns, leaving net sales unchanged; and (4) hybrid information-emotion FGUC increases sales more than returns, improving net sales. Mechanism analyses indicate that emotion-focused FGUC heightens arousal and shortens deliberation time, triggering impulse purchases that are often subsequently returned. In contrast, hybrid information-emotion FGUC balances emotion with information, ultimately boosting net sales. Additional analyses show that scarcity cues embedded in FGUC exert the strongest influence on purchase behavior.

title: Digital Infrastructure in Thin Markets: Evidence from a Tribal-led Broadband Rollout
affiliations: and George Mason University - Buchanan Center Political Economy

detail.title: Digital Infrastructure in Thin Markets: Evidence from a Tribal-led Broadband Rollout
detail.abstract: When do broadband investments generate large economic returns? We estimate the effects of a tribal-led broadband rollout on the Colville Reservation in Washington State, a thin market with near-zero baseline connectivity. In 2013, the tribal government began expanding service in a sequence shaped by line-of-sight, power availability, and cross-government approvals. Our main design uses a reservationlevel synthetic control with ACS five-year estimates, complemented by a ZIP-area difference-indifferences design using annual administrative data. Relative to synthetic Colville, American Indian per-capita income rises by about $5,500 in 2016 dollars, labor force participation by 10.3 percentage points, and the employed share by 6.1 percentage points. ZIP-area estimates indicate higher adjusted gross income per return, wages per return, and paid employment at establishments. Mechanism checks are most consistent with center-mediated access and use by public and tribaladjacent organizations rather than broad household subscription or in-migration. Public sector employment rises where the tribal administrative center is located. By contrast, measured household subscription and population do not rise relative to counterfactuals.

title: Facilitate or Backfire? Streamer Happiness and Product Sales Performance in Livestream Shopping

detail.title: Facilitate or Backfire? Streamer Happiness and Product Sales Performance in Livestream Shopping
detail.abstract: Does streamer happiness facilitate or backfire on monetized consumption in livestream shopping? Prior evidence is mixed: it increases monetary tipping in entertainment livestreaming but appears to reduce product sales in television-based shopping. The authors revisit this tension by examining the role of streamer happiness in livestream shopping. Leveraging state-of-the-art facial expression analysis, the authors extract over 33 million frame-level emotion measures from 126,376 minutes of livestream video on TikTok and match them to actual sales data. Exploiting within-product-livestreamstreamer-presentation variation in streamer happiness, the authors find that a onestandard-deviation increase in streamer happiness is associated with an average 11.2% increase in product net sales, a result that is robust to alternative specifications and an instrumental variable approach. Mechanism analyses suggest that this effect operates through uncertainty reduction and emotional contagion: the effect is stronger under higher product uncertainty, and higher happiness increases positive, high-arousal, and emoji-rich comments. Interestingly, the sales effect does not vary with the intensity of Duchenne (i.e., authentic) smiles, implying that professionally performed smiles can also be economically effective. Taken together, these findings shed light on how livestream agencies, brand merchants, and streamers can manage emotional display to improve product sales performance in livestream shopping.

title: Impact of Money Laundering on Economic System: International Legal Framework and Corresponding Development in Pakistan

detail.title: Impact of Money Laundering on Economic System: International Legal Framework and Corresponding Development in Pakistan
detail.abstract: This doctrinal mode study, based on the “Black Letter Law Method” aimed to identify the socio-economic existence, impacts, and severity of offence of Money Laundering (ML) and global regulatory response to cope with various emerging forms of ML. The study further aimed to analyze the legislative upgradations and legal setup of the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regime in Pakistan. The operational and governance model of its Financial Intelligence Unit was also examined as well as its capacity to cope with trade-based ML offences in purview of modern practices. The study concluded that ML is an offence as much as a social norm affecting the economy through its various predicate and derivative offences and socially deep-rooted forms. Major over-hauling in operational and enforcement regime of the current Anti-Money Laundering Law of Pakistan is necessarily required. This is because it is not effective in timely detecting and combating the growing trends of ML related offences in a country striving for better economic performance, specifically offences pertaining to trade-based money laundering (TBML). The administrative model of the Financial Intelligence Unit of Pakistan, also known as the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU), is governed under the AML Act 2020. It holds various lacunas in terms of the lack of horizontal coordination mechanism among the reporting entities, as well as centralized administrative control of FMU by the political representatives which hinders its operational, administrative, and regulatory autonomy. Moreover, there is insufficient technical expertise within the regulatory mechanism as well as incomplete and ineffective regulatory coverage over a number of business and financial sectors within the jurisdiction, coupled with the absence of standardized regulations, and non-enrollment of FMU by a global governing body.

detail.abstract: We compare continuous double auctions and periodic uniform-price batch auctions on a fixed exogenous order path. The two mechanisms optimize different objectives even when they receive the same orders. Continuous trading matches greedily over time; periodic auctions wait and select high-bid, low-ask pairs from a larger pool. We prove two pathwise refinement theorems. First, for non-expiring limit orders, refining the clearing calendar weakly increases executed trade quantity; the statement is unchanged if market orders are represented as resting extreme limits. Hence the continuous double auction executes weakly more quantity than any periodic auction. Second, with finite reservation prices, coarsening the clearing calendar weakly increases reservation-spread surplus, equivalently aggregate price improvement summed across both sides of each trade. Thus periodic auctions weakly dominate continuous trading on aggregate price improvement. Both comparisons require nested calendar refinement; numerical interval length alone does not order outcomes. The two results identify a mechanical quantity-surplus tradeoff: continuous markets support more execution by using more pricing opportunities, while batch auctions concentrate execution on wider-spread pairs. Notional volume traded sits outside this ranking: because it depends on transaction prices as well as matches, natural pricing conventions can make notional volume favor either mechanism.

title: Parametric Catastrophe Tokens as an On-chain Risk Transfer Instrument A Framework for Deflationary Supply Mechanics Linked to Verified Catastrophe Losses

detail.title: Parametric Catastrophe Tokens as an On-chain Risk Transfer Instrument A Framework for Deflationary Supply Mechanics Linked to Verified Catastrophe Losses

detail.abstract: The global protection gap-the difference between economic losses from natural catastrophes and insured losses-reached $257 billion in 2024. Traditional insurance and Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS) structures have not closed this gap, partly because they require sophisticated investors with minimum capital thresholds and bilateral contractual arrangements. This paper proposes and formally analyses a new class of instrument: the parametric catastrophe token, called PACE (Portfolio Aggregate Catastrophe Exposure). A PACE token is a digital asset whose supply is permanently and automatically reduced whenever a qualifying disaster is verified by an independent oracle. The governing formula is: Tokens Burned = MIN(Loss × s, Reserve × 5%), where Loss is the verified total economic loss in dollars above a $100M franchise threshold, s is a fixed sensitivity parameter derived from the 95th percentile of historical individual event losses for each specific scenario, and the second term provides a tail-risk safety cap. We root the valuation mechanics in established corporate finance theory: the Protocol Burn Reserve constitutes a dilution overhang, and its permanent reduction through burns is structurally equivalent to a non-discretionary share buyback. We prove three formal properties-loss proportionality, inflation invariance, and reserve self-limitation-and validate them against 25 years of EM-DAT data (2000-2024). The safety cap binds in 1-5 out of 25 historical years per scenario, corresponding consistently to recognised major catastrophe events.

title: Adversarial Implementation and Instantaneous Convergence: A New Paradigm for Mechanism Design

detail.title: Adversarial Implementation and Instantaneous Convergence: A New Paradigm for Mechanism Design
detail.abstract: We formalize a dynamic intervention protocol designed to resolve collective action problems in high-dimensional environments. Traditional economic paradigms-such as Pigouvian taxes, Coasean bargaining, and repeated games-are constrained by physical limits, including administrative costs, transaction costs, and transition time friction that scale with population size. This paper proposes a new paradigm that decouples expectation management from the underlying penalty structure. By introducing an exogenous initial reward pool to break symmetry, coupled with a state-dependent exponential penalty (γ(k) = α ^(N-k)), the mechanism dismantles the common knowledge of the Pareto-suboptimal Nash equilibrium. Under the strict assumption of rationality, the mechanism utilizes "Phantom Deterrence" on off-equilibrium paths, forcing the system to instantaneously converge to the globally optimal state. The core contribution of this framework is that, while requiring a fixed ignition cost, its marginal execution cost is strictly zero. This asymptotically eliminates average costs in large populations, fundamentally bypassing the scale frictions of traditional paradigms and providing a rigorous theoretical bound for evaluating institutional efficiency.

detail.abstract: This study examines the practical exploitability of the overnight market anomaly in Indian equity markets using index futures. While prior research [4][12] suggests that most equity returns are generated outside trading hours, the economic viability remains uncertain once transaction costs, slippage, and taxes are accounted for. Using the past six-year historical data of the NIFTY future contracts to backtest a systematic trading strategy that maintains long exposure exclusively during overnight periods, entering positions near the market close and exiting them at the subsequent market open. The performance of the strategy is evaluated relative to a passive buy-and-hold exposure to the NIFTY Index and assessed using cumulative returns, volatility, Sharpe ratio [11], maximum drawdown [8], and risk-adjusted performance measures.
